fixes.explanation: That's the one, friend. Asaph says it three ways: "…be not silent; be not speechless; be not still, O God." I bet he's worried, because when you're worried, one way to say it just isn't enough. I think he's asking God to speak up and act.
I see why you'd pick it, friend, but impatient isn't the word he uses. He says "…be not silent; be not speechless; be not still, O God." Three ways of asking God not to stay quiet.
I get why you'd guess it, but fear isn't the word. Asaph says the enemies scheme "with cunning." That means they're sneaky and planning ahead. I'd rather not meet anyone who schemes like that.

Not the king this time, friend! Asaph is talking to God, so when he says "they form an alliance against You…" the "You" is God Himself. All those nations teaming up, and the target is God. Wild, right?
The high priest doesn't show up anywhere in this psalm, friend. Asaph is praying to God, and he says "they form an alliance against You…" That "You" is God Himself.

Yes, the pastures of God. The psalm has some people saying, "Let us possess for ourselves the pastures of God." Whoever said it wanted something that belonged to God. They'd have done better to ask for a cookie.

Gold! Everybody reaches for the gold, friend, but Ophir's gold isn't in this verse. The quote is "Let us possess for ourselves the pastures of God." Shiny stuff wasn't the goal here. The psalm says pastures, and it calls them God's.
